question: Which genetic combination is most commonly found in biological males?

options.C: One X and one Y chromosome

explanation: Great job! Biological males usually inherit an X chromosome from the mother and a Y chromosome from the father, giving an XY pairing. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why can assigning biological sex at birth based only on external genitals sometimes be tricky?

options.A: Hormone levels are impossible to measure in newborns
options.B: External genitalia change completely during the first year of life
options.C: Chromosomes are always identical in every human being
options.D: Internal organs and chromosomes can occasionally differ from external physical appearance

explanation: You've got this! Genitals are just one part of biological sex; variations in chromosomes or internal anatomy mean external looks don't always tell the whole story. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h1)

question: What phrase best describes a person's gender identity?

options.A: The legal documents issued by the government
options.B: Their internal, deeply felt sense of their own gender
options.C: The specific sex chromosomes they inherited at birth
options.D: The physical clothes and style they choose to wear

explanation: Spot on! Gender identity is internal and psychological—it's how individuals perceive themselves on the inside. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h2)

question: How is gender expression different from gender identity?

options.A: Expression is the outward display of gender, while identity is the internal feeling
options.B: Expression has no connection to societal rules, unlike identity
options.C: Expression is fixed at birth, while identity changes daily
options.D: Expression refers only to chromosomes, while identity refers to hormones

explanation: Exactly right! Gender expression is what others can see (like clothing and behavior), whereas gender identity is a private, internal experience. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h2)

question: Which of these is a social and cultural concept rather than a purely biological one?
explanation: Well done! Gender involves societal roles and identities, while chromosomes and physical organs are purely biological. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why must nurses carefully separate the concepts of sex and gender during patient assessments?

options.B: To diagnose chromosomal disorders more cheaply
options.C: To avoid making false clinical assumptions about a patient based only on their anatomy
options.D: To ensure laboratory tests run faster

explanation: Brilliant! Knowing the difference stops us from stereotyping patients and helps us give safe, individualized care. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h3)

question: What does the term 'intersex' mean in human biology?

options.A: Biological variations where reproductive anatomy or chromosomes do not fit typical male or female definitions
options.B: A person whose gender identity changes every few months
options.C: The exact midpoint between two different cultural gender roles
options.D: An individual who takes hormone replacement therapy later in life

explanation: Spot on! Intersex simply describes physical or genetic traits that don' strictly align with standard male or female definitions. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is the modern medical approach to non-urgent surgeries on intersex infants?

options.A: Delaying non-urgent procedures to protect bodily autonomy until the child can participate
options.B: Mandating hormone therapy immediately after birth
options.C: Ignoring the physical variation completely without any documentation
options.D: Performing immediate surgery on every infant to fix chromosomal imbalances

explanation: You got it! Modern medical ethics value a child's right to their own body, avoiding rushed, irreversible cosmetic surgeries. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h4)

question: What do we mean by the term 'gender roles'?

options.A: The legal medical definitions used in hospitals
options.B: The specific genetic markers found on human chromosomes
options.C: Societal expectations and behaviors considered appropriate for men and women
options.D: The biological hormones produced by the endocrine glands

explanation: Correct! Gender roles are the cultural rules and tasks society assigns based on perceived gender. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why is it correct to say gender roles are social constructs?

options.A: Because they are identical in every country across the world
options.B: Because they depend strictly on the presence of the Y chromosome
options.C: Because they are permanently encoded in human DNA at conception
options.D: Because they are created by human cultures and change across different times and places

explanation: Well done! Because they are human-made rules, gender roles change from culture to culture and shift over time. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h5)

question: How can biological sex directly affect how a patient responds to medication?

options.A: By changing the patient's personal gender identity overnight
options.B: By eliminating all potential drug side effects completely
options.C: By affecting how medications are metabolized and cleared in the body
options.D: By determining the exact cost of the prescription at the pharmacy

explanation: Spot on! Differences in organ size, body fat, and enzymes mean drugs can clear differently in male and female bodies. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h6)

question: A male patient with severe chest pain waited three days to visit the clinic because he felt he had to 'be strong' for his family. Which concept best explains this delay?

options.A: An innate genetic flaw in male chromosome pairing
options.B: Socially constructed gender roles influencing health-seeking behavior
options.C: A standard physiological reaction to low blood pressure
options.D: An intersex hormonal imbalance affecting pain receptors

explanation: You're doing great! Traditional masculine expectations to be stoic can sadly stop men from seeking quick medical attention. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is a crucial first step for nurses who want to provide gender-sensitive care?

options.A: Changing the legal laws of the country immediately
options.B: Ignoring all cultural traditions practiced by patients
options.C: Prescribing higher doses of medication to male patients
options.D: Reflecting on personal cultural biases and stereotypes

explanation: Exactly! Self-reflection helps us spot our own hidden biases so we can treat every patient with professional respect. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a good strategy for promoting gender-sensitive nursing care?

options.A: Considering both biological factors and social pressures during assessment
options.B: Using respectful and inclusive language during patient history collection
options.C: Making automatic assumptions about a patient's health needs based purely on their gender
options.D: Advocating for equitable healthcare access across all segments of society

explanation: Spot on! Good nursing care means treating every patient as a unique individual, not making assumptions based on gender stereotypes. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T2#GNS312_U4_T2_h7)
